So, after basically copying everything from here, making a map in Tiled, and installing XRANDR (because I'm a moron) I got the screenshot linked above. It filled me with a joy kids get when Christmas morning rolls around.

Now, for the meat of this post. Along with this vlog, I set up a Trello board to have a way to check off things the prototype engine needs so the game can be in a horridly running state. My first focus is modifying the TiledMap that LibGDX supplies so I can make my maps more dynamic without making 4000 different maps. I plan on using something like what Minecraft does with it's grass blocks, grayscale the texture and use a color map to programmatically layer a color over it. That should cut down a good chunk of the Tileset I would need to ship with this game while having a lot of room to "add" new things. Seeing as we've got some downtime, now I can write this. I just want to preface this with three things: a.) I don't reside in Tropia, b.) most of my account of this is from the chat log. I didn't actually go to Tropia to see the "bridge," and c.) I started drinking after the incident, but before writing this, so I hope it makes sense.

I was somewhat disappointed in how the community handled TheIdSay (or whoever they were) and bridge across Tropia's lake. While IdSay was definitely wrong and was being obstinate about it, a lot of the ostracizing and piling on that occurred as the incident continued was unnecessary and mostly immature.

For those who weren't here, user TheIdSay (sp?) had what I think were one-block bridges (and mentioned something about railroad tracks) crossing the main lake of Tropia to make it easier to cross. Now, this is against the rules in Tropia by default. You aren't allowed to build on the lake, and you aren't supposed to build without running it past Duey first, I believe. IdSay claimed that Duey was the times they wanted to run it by them, and worked on it anyway. Now, normally someone would just break those blocks, but IdSay ended up claiming their build on top of the lake. As an outsider, this seemed like a cardinal sin in Tropia, and IdSay was met with backlash. And rightfully so, IdSay had broken the few rules that Tropia has, posted on signs for all to see when they /warp there.

Everything started off somewhat reasonable. Some people were complaining and asking about the bridge, and IdSay started out by complaining about people destroying their stuff in Tropia. As IdSay tried to use flimsy excuses as a defense and the community rebuked one after another, the community slowly and slowly began getting more frustrated. Mods had weighed in against IdSay a few times, and just about every excuse IdSay had a rebuttal, except for their insistence to talk to Duey. Even though people claim to have gotten an answer from him from Skype, IdSay was having none of that and insisted on waiting to talk to Duey to do anything (despite not waiting to see Duey to build in the first place).

Now, this meantime is where I start to become more disappointed with how this is being handled by my fellow players. At this point, it's obvious that the problem person is not processing the fact that maybe when the entire community and a mod or two disagrees with you that you should reconsider your position. And instead of simply leaving the bridge alone and letting Duey give that person get a smackdown, some people continued to drag out the situation and become increasingly hostile in chat. Eventually, mod-hero Xerox stepped in and handled it, muting TheIdSay until they could resolve the situation with Duey. The piling on that user didn't stop after Xerox stepped in and muted them, though, others continued popping shots at the user. Soon after, that user got to plead his case to Duey and got shot down, afterwards people were bringing up him out of nowhere, one member took to calling them "town idiot", and more.

While I understand why members of our community were getting frustrated (I know I was!), it doesn't mean we should be ALL CAPS SHOUTING and asking for them to be banned, permission to kill them, etc. That was some low shit. Even worse, there were at least a half-dozen players joining our server during all of the drama in chat, and all I could think was, "This really isn't the environment a new player should join into..." In my opinion, chat actually sank below TheIdSay's level, no matter how wrong that user was. Overall, it was really petty and kinda disappointing to see. This is the first community I've really cared for a while, and I want to see it flourish. Tonight, the environment created was counterproductive to that. We need to try to be respectful, mature adults in the face of conflict, and I hope we can hold each other to a higher standard.
